# Claude session transcript: MAIIC feeds and E-Banker integration

This is the complete record of the part of a Claude Code session (9 to 14 October 2026) that followed the audit closure of 9 October. It is saved so that another member of staff, with or without an AI tool, can follow what was done, in what order, and why. The earlier part of the same session is in Claude_Session_Transcript_Audit_Closure_2026-10-09.

It starts at the question about SQL Developer's "result set exceeds the maximum size (100 MB)" message and runs to the saving of this transcript. The work falls into five stages, in time order:
1. Pack 3 and the 9 October returns: the SPOOL note for large exports, the RUN 0 date-format check, the Mega Farm runs, method A against method B, write-offs, the feed route setting and the arrears data.
2. Packs 7 to 9: the pack 7 results review, OVERDUE_DETAILS added as RUN 8 with its goal stated, the 100 MB failure and the split into 8a, 8b and 8c, and the pack 9 results review (CV_10 is the migration worksheet; CV_14 ties the old ledger to the GL).
3. The December 2025 ECL models against the RBM DFI Directive 2018: how the directive was applied in the models compared with the system.
4. The E-Banker integration pack: the five feed routes, the landing zone and its four tables, the endpoint (route 3), the bootstrap as the test harness, the read-only account set-up with a connection test, configuration and security, refresh, duplicates, governance, storage and backup, a dated timetable, pack 10 in the register, the system's move onto MAIIC's server, and the plain-language guide.
5. The documents humanised by two editor agents, checked against snapshots, rendered with a logo, justified text and a table of contents, and saved.

What is included: every user message, every reply shown to the user, every tool call with its full input (commands, scripts and file contents), and every tool result in full. Where a long result was stored by the tooling in a side file, that file is reproduced here.

What is left out: the assistant's internal reasoning, automatic system reminders, and image outputs (page renders used for visual checks).

How to follow it: the integration documents and figures are in 3. Project Execution/E-Banker Integration; the scripts that made them are in Build files/2026-10-14 next to this transcript, with a README, and in docs/build-files in the repository.

Times are UTC. Source: the session log ee984144-7b28-4df1-9a6e-560f112869e9.jsonl, entries 10596 to 12761. Events: 755.

## USER  (2026-10-09 10:06:40 UTC)

if in sql developer an error message says result set exceeds the maximum size (100mb) if necessary you can explicitly continue this query. what does that mean and what do I need to do


## CLAUDE  (2026-10-09 10:07:10 UTC)

**What it means**

SQL Developer caps how much of a result it will hold in memory for the grid — by default 100 MB. When a query returns more than that (MF_03, the Mega Farm ledger, is exactly the file I warned would be "several times the MAIIC ledger"), it stops fetching and shows that message. Nothing is wrong with the query or the database; the tool has simply stopped reading rows. If you exported at that point you'd get a **truncated file** with no warning in it — the most dangerous outcome, because it looks complete.

**What to do — three options, best first**

1. **Raise the limit once, then re-run.**
   Tools → Preferences → Database → Advanced → *"Result Set Fetch Size"* is not it; the one you want is Tools → Preferences → Database → Worksheet → **"Max rows to print in a script"** *(for script output)* and, for the grid, Preferences → Database → Advanced → **"SQL Array Fetch Size"** is unrelated — the setting that governs this message is:
   **Tools → Preferences → Database → Worksheet → "Maximum size of result set to store in memory (MB)"** (in some versions under Database → Advanced). Set it to 1000, click OK, re-run the query, then export. The message disappears for anything under the new cap.

2. **Export without the grid at all — the cleanest for a big file.**
   Instead of running the query and exporting the grid, use the spool approach in the worksheet, which streams straight to disk and has no memory cap:
   ```sql
   SET SQLFORMAT csv
   SPOOL C:\exports\MF_03_ledger_all.csv
   SELECT cv.* FROM cumvouch cv WHERE ... ORDER BY ...;   -- the RUN 4 query as written
   SPOOL OFF
   ```
   Run it with **Run Script (F5)**, not Run Statement. RUN 0 still applies to the session first. (Headers are included in csv format; one caveat: `SET SQLFORMAT csv` quotes strings and leaves numbers bare, which is what we want.)

3. **Accept the "continue" and keep going.** The message's "explicitly continue this query" means scroll to the bottom of the grid and SQL Developer will fetch the next batch; keep doing that until it stops, then export. Workable, but easy to export too early — I'd avoid it for MF_03.

**Which to use:** option 2 for MF_03 (and MF_04 if it's large); option 1 is fine for everything else. Either way, after exporting, open the CSV and check the last row is a real row (ends with a complete quoted line), and tell us the row count — the system's gates compare it with the count in the manifest, so a truncated file will be refused rather than silently landed.

Want me to add a "big files" box with the SPOOL block to the pack-3 run sheet?

file_path: C:\Users\wadza\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\2. Documents from clients\Raw Query Scripts\Query Requests to MAIIC\Received 9 October\Pack 3\BIG FILES - export MF_03 with SPOOL (result set exceeds 100 MB).txt
--- content ---
BIG FILES - EXPORT WITH SPOOL  |  Dupleix Institute  |  9 October 2026

Why: SQL Developer holds at most 100 MB of a result in its grid. A bigger
result (the Mega Farm ledger, MF_03) stops with "result set exceeds the
maximum size (100 MB)", and an export taken then is a TRUNCATED file that
looks complete. SPOOL writes straight to disk with no size cap.

How: paste the block below into the worksheet and run it with RUN SCRIPT
(F5), not Run Statement. Create the folder C:\exports first (or change the
path). RUN 0 still comes first in the same worksheet.

-- RUN 0 (once, first)
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_DATE_FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS';
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS = '.,';

-- MF_03: the Mega Farm ledger (RUN 4 of the pack-3 sheet, unchanged)
SET SQLFORMAT csv
SPOOL C:\exports\MF_03_ledger_all.csv
SELECT cv.*
FROM   cumvouch cv
WHERE  cv.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                            WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103))
ORDER  BY cv.new_ac_number, cv.transaction_date, cv.cumvouch_det_id;
SPOOL OFF

-- MF_04: the Mega Farm balance history, the same way if it is also large
SET SQLFORMAT csv
SPOOL C:\exports\MF_04_balance_history.csv
SELECT b.*
FROM   account_balance b
WHERE  b.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (96,97,98,99,100,101,102,103))
AND    b.transaction_date = LAST_DAY(b.transaction_date)
ORDER  BY b.new_ac_number, b.transaction_date;
SPOOL OFF

SET SQLFORMAT default

Notes
- SQLFORMAT csv writes a header row, quotes strings and leaves numbers bare:
  the same shape as the other files.
- One SELECT per SPOOL block, one file each. Do not put two SELECTs between
  one SPOOL and SPOOL OFF.
- If the first line of the file repeats the SQL text, that is the worksheet
  echo: it does no harm, but SET ECHO OFF before SPOOL removes it.
- When done, open the file and check the LAST row is a complete quoted row,
  and send the row count with the file: the system's gates compare it with
  the manifest and refuse a short file rather than land it.
- Alternative for smaller results: Tools > Preferences > Database > Worksheet,
  raise "Maximum size of result set to store in memory (MB)" to 1000, re-run,
  then Export Data as usual.

````

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-13 12:54:14 UTC)

The system already has the integration designed and three of its five routes built (spec v4 section 6.5), so "integrate" means choosing the route MAIIC can run and switching it on. The steps, in order:

**Step 1 — Fix the extracts as the interface (done, keep stable)**
The 18 queries in the register (`EbankerQuerySeeder`: P1_01 ledger, P1_02/03 masters, P2_09 balances, P2_08 loan-book runs, etc.) *are* the integration contract. Every route delivers the same files to the same door (`PackLandingService`) through the same gates. Any change to a query is a version bump in the register, which the gate checks (M2e). So the first step is simply: no more ad-hoc exports — the pack is the thing.

**Step 2 — Get the session settings right, once (RUN 0)**
Every route below runs the same SQL; it must run with `NLS_DATE_FORMAT` ISO and point decimals. In a scheduled or programmatic route this is set in the script, not by hand, which is exactly why routes 2–5 are better than a person in SQL Developer.

**Step 3 — Choose the route. The realistic ladder:**

| Route | What it is | Status | What MAIIC must do |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Manual upload | Barry exports, someone uploads the zip on the Feed screen | Built | Nothing — it's what we do now. Fine for month-end, wrong for daily |
| **2 Scheduled export** | A SQLcl script on a MAIIC machine runs the register's queries on a schedule, zips them with a manifest (hashes, counts), drops the zip in a shared folder; the system polls it daily (`eir:poll-feed-folder`, 06:30) | Built; template at `docs/bootstrap/queries/Route 2 - scheduled export (SQLcl) - template.sql` | ICT installs SQLcl + a read-only DB account on one server, schedules the script (Windows Task Scheduler), shares the drop folder with the app server |
| 3 API push | The same script posts the zip to `POST /api/ebanker-feed/pack` with a bearer token over HTTPS | Built (token constant-time, zip guarded) | As route 2 plus HTTPS on the app server and the token in both `.env` files |
| 4 Direct read | The app reads the Oracle views itself over the VPN with a read-only account | Designed, not built | ICT's consent to a read-only Oracle account reachable from the app server; the Oracle client on it |
| 5 Vendor view/API | Virtual Galaxy builds and supports a view or API | Not built | A paid change request to the vendor; months |

**My recommendation: route 2 now, route 3 when HTTPS is in place, route 4 only if ICT offers it.** Route 2 needs nothing from the vendor, no new network path into the core, and gives MAIIC a daily pack with a manifest they can audit.

**Step 4 — The route-2 checklist for Barry (one afternoon)**
1. A read-only Oracle user for the extracts (SELECT on the 18 tables; nothing else) — ICT's own control, and what the audit's D22/D23 assume.
2. SQLcl installed on a MAIIC server that can see the database.
3. Our template script with the account name and drop folder filled in; it writes the pack name `pack_YYYY-MM-DD`, each CSV, and `manifest.json` with SHA-256 and row counts — the gates need both.
4. A scheduled task: daily at 05:00 (so the 06:30 poll finds it), monthly on the 1st for the month-end files. The incremental queries use the watermark ids the system last recorded (it prints them on the Feed screen).
5. The drop folder shared to the app server (a UNC path in `config/services.php` → `ebanker_feed.folder`).
6. One dry run: Barry runs the script by hand, we land the pack with `eir:land-pack --dry-run`, read the gate results, fix anything (usually dates), then switch the schedule on.

**Step 5 — Governance switch**
Set `ebanker_feed_route` in the Governance Centre to the route in force (proposed, approved by a second person). The audit noted the poller only prints this setting today (M12 wiring for that key is still open) — a small finish I'd do when the route is chosen.

**Step 6 — Prove it on the first month**
The first month-end through the route is run twice: once by the route, once by Barry's manual pack. The gates must say the two land identically (same hashes, same counts) and method B must tie to the stored report as it does now. That's the acceptance test; after it, manual packs stop.

**Step 7 — Only then, the engines on a schedule**
Once packs arrive on their own, `eir:build-loan-books` and the staging/PD/LGD/ECL chain run from the scheduler after each month-end landing, under maker-checker for the build approval. Nothing new to build there — the commands exist; it's a `Kernel.php` schedule line and a decision on who approves.

**What needs MAIIC before any of this moves:** ICT's read-only account (step 4.1) and a server for the script (4.2). Everything else is ours. If you want, I'll draft the one-page request to ICT for those two things, with the exact grants.

how are we to get the loanbooks in?


## CLAUDE  (2026-10-13 12:57:15 UTC)

The loan book isn't imported as a file any more — it's **built from the landed pack**, which is the point of the spec's section 6.2. Three methods exist; the governed setting `loan_book_build_method` says which is in force (B today).

**What "getting the loan book in" means now**

| Method | Source | When |
|---|---|---|
| **B — derived from the ledger** (the one in force) | The landed ledger (P1_01 / M09_xx), the masters and the rate set-up: carrying amount = the signed sum of every posting on the account; arrears from the stored run; DPD from the overdue date | Every month. This is the one that ties to the stored report on 2,361 of 2,361 account-months and to the GL to the cent |
| **A — the stored report** | E-Banker's own Loan Book Report runs (P2_08 / M09_03): latest run per account per month-end | The control against B; and the source of arrears buckets |
| **C — the Excel report** | The monthly Excel MAIIC produced before the pack existed, landed by hash with a date gate | Only for a month where there's no pack — history before the extracts, or an emergency |

**The monthly routine, concretely**

1. **Land the month's pack** — by whichever feed route is in force (today: Barry's files uploaded on the Feed screen, or `php artisan eir:land-pack <folder>`). The gates check hashes, counts, dates, keys, account-in-master, the balance-history tie, the month-end rows. A failed gate quarantines the pack with the reason; nothing is built from it.
2. **Build the month** — `php artisan eir:build-loan-books 2026-09 2026-09` (or the Build button on the Feed screen). The build writes method B's rows, compares them with method A's stored run, and prints every difference above two cents before anyone approves.
3. **Approve under maker-checker** — a different person from the requester, on the screen. The build records its method, its pack and its approver on every row.
4. **Lock the period** — `eir:lock-period 2026-09` once the month is accepted; after that no engine can restate it (the audit's H4).
5. Then the engines run on it (staging → PD/LGD → ECL → revenue) — in the bootstrap order, or from the scheduler once the feed is automatic.

**Where we are with September specifically**

M09_01 (ledger since August) and M09_02 (balances) landed on 8 October and passed; M09_03 (the 30 September report run) arrived on 9 October. That's everything method B and method A need for September. Nothing is stopping us building it now:

```
php artisan --env=bootstrap eir:land-pack "<Received 9 October>"   (M09_03 only)
php artisan --env=bootstrap eir:build-loan-books 2026-09 2026-09
```

and reading the A-vs-B comparison — the first live month-end through the door. Want me to do that?


## USER  (2026-10-13 12:58:32 UTC)

Whats method A?


## CLAUDE  (2026-10-13 12:58:45 UTC)

**Method A takes E-Banker's own Loan Book Report as the loan book.**

E-Banker has a report called the Loan Book Report. Every time someone runs it, the system stores the result as a set of rows — one per account, dated with an "as-on" date — in the table `LOAN_BOOK_DETAILS_ALL`. That's what the extract P2_08 (and the monthly M09_03) pulls: the stored runs, not a fresh calculation.

Method A reads those stored runs and, for each month-end, takes **the latest run per account with that as-on date**. Its columns become the loan-book row directly: approved amount, disbursed, principal, interest to date, carrying amount, the arrears buckets (1–30, 31–90, 91–180, 180–270, 271–360), the overdue date, the rate, the tenor. Nothing is computed; it is "what E-Banker said the book was on that day".

Two things to know about it:

- **It's a snapshot, so it only exists where someone ran the report.** For months before December 2024 there are no stored runs, so method A derives those months and marks them as derived. September 2026 has runs on 24, 28, 29 and 30 September (two on the 30th, both executed on 1 October); method A takes the latest 30 September run.
- **It can't be audited back to postings.** A figure in the report is whatever the report's own logic produced; if the report is wrong (the Zaithwa Farms balance rows are the known case), method A carries the error. That's why **method B** — the carrying amount as the signed sum of every ledger posting — is the one in force, and **method A is the control**: the build computes B, lays A beside it, and prints every account-month where they differ by more than two cents. On the committed history they agree on 2,361 of 2,361 account-months (one cent on one), which is the proof that B reproduces the bank's own book from its postings.

So: A = the report as stored; B = the book rebuilt from the ledger; A checks B every month. Method C is only for a month with no pack at all (the Excel the report used to be exported to, landed by hash).

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-13 14:07:48 UTC)

**From the ledger — not from a write-off table.** There is no write-off import. A write-off reaches the system as a posting in E-Banker's ledger (`CUMVOUCH`, extract P1_01) with transaction type **300**, and the landed ledger is where every engine reads it.

Where it goes from there:

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Landing | P1_01 lands like any ledger row; the two write-offs in the committed pack are type 300 on Micholess Creameries and Maluso Cooperative, 22.3m, narrated "By Trf … Write off" |
| Loan-book build (`LoanBookBuildService`, `TYPE_WRITEOFF`) | The posting stays in the carrying amount (the balance is the signed sum of every posting, so the write-off credit reduces it) but is kept **out of repayments** — it isn't cash (audit H1, fixed 9 Oct) |
| EIR inputs (`ContractInputsBuildService`) | Carried into `eir_actual_transactions` as a `Write-off` transaction |
| Revenue roll-forward (`EirRevenueService`) | Taken off the gross as derecognition, disclosed on the row, never as cash received |
| LGD workout (`LgdEngineService`) | A loan absent from the end book is treated as written off (recovery nil) unless its last row shows it settled |
| Reports / FS note | Appear in the gross-carrying movement and the note's write-off line |

**Why not E-Banker's write-off table:** the schema has `LOAN_WRITEOFF_MASTER` / `LOAN_WRITEOFF_TRANS` (the dictionary even has a sample header: write-off date, amount, remarks, workable flag), but the 6 October row counts showed both **empty** — MAIIC appears to write off by ledger transfer, not through that module. Pack 3's RUN 7 (CT_01) asks Barry for the counts again, and RUN 10 (WO_01) extracts the table only if it holds rows for our schemes. If it ever does, those rows would add the *reason and date of decision*; the amount and the accounting would still come from the type-300 posting.

**Two things to be aware of:** the directive's section 12 requires a loss-classified facility to be written off in the following quarter — the system can report candidates (Loss class on the RBM return) but the write-off itself remains a MAIIC posting; and write-offs are also one of the reasons the audit's D20 control-exception list matters, since a write-off posted without the allowance having been raised would show up as a gross movement with no provision release.

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-13 14:21:55 UTC)

**The route itself is a governed setting**, changed on the screen, not in a file:

**Governance Centre → the setting `ebanker_feed_route`** ("How E-Banker data arrives: the feed route"), options Route 1 manual upload (the default and today's) / Route 2 scheduled folder / Route 3 API push / Route 4 direct read / Route 5 vendor view. Like every setting it's changed by **propose** (with a reason and an effective date) and **approve** by a different person; the audit trail records who and when, and the trace shows the route in force for each month.

What each route needs beside the setting:

| Route | Where else |
|---|---|
| 1 Manual upload | Nothing: Data Foundation → E-Banker Feed → Upload pack |
| 2 Scheduled folder | `.env`: `EBANKER_FEED_FOLDER=` the drop folder (UNC path); the poll time is `app/Console/Kernel.php` line 29 (`eir:poll-feed-folder`, daily 06:30); the export script on Barry's side is `docs/bootstrap/queries/Route 2 - scheduled export (SQLcl) - template.sql` |
| 3 API push | `.env`: `EBANKER_FEED_TOKEN=` the bearer token (the same value in the export script); HTTPS on the app server; the endpoint is `POST /api/ebanker-feed/pack` |
| 4 / 5 | Not built yet; the setting can name them but nothing runs until they are |

**The queries the feed runs** (the other sense of "changing the feed") are in the register — Data Foundation → E-Banker Feed → Queries tab, seeded from `database/seeders/EbankerQuerySeeder.php`. Changing a query means a new version there; the gate (M2e) refuses a pack whose manifest states a version the register doesn't know.

One honest caveat from the audit (M12): today the poller reads `ebanker_feed_route` only to print it — it polls the folder and the API inbox daily regardless of the setting. So the setting is the record of the route in force and the control a second person approves, but it doesn't yet switch the poller off and on. That's a small wiring item I can finish when MAIIC chooses the route.

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-13 15:26:35 UTC)

Both, in this order:

**1. The landed copy (raw, as E-Banker reported it)** — `ebanker_raw_rows` with `query_id = P2_08` (and M09_03 for September). Each stored Loan Book Report run carries the arrears as E-Banker computed them on that day: the five buckets `DAY_1_30, DAY_31_91, DAY_91_180, DAY_181_270, DAY_271_360`, plus `OVERDUE_PRINCI_DATE` (the date of the oldest overdue instalment), `OVERDUE_PERIOD` and `INSTALLMENT_AMT`. That's the source table; it's append-only and versioned with its pack, so the arrears "as reported" for any month-end are always recoverable. There's no separately normalised arrears table — the raw run row is the record.

**2. The loan book (built)** — `loan_books` carries `arrears_1_to_30 … arrears_271_to_360`, `overdue_principal_date`, `overdue_status`, and `overdue_days`. The build copies the buckets and the overdue date from the latest stored run for the month-end, then computes **DPD** itself under the governed `dpd_basis`: days from `OVERDUE_PRINCI_DATE` to the month-end (the directive's basis), with the bucket's lower bound as the fallback when the date is blank. Staging reads that DPD; the four-instalment trigger comes from a different pair of sources (the instalment chart P2_10 against ledger receipts), not from the buckets.

Two things to know:

- **E-Banker's bucket edges aren't the directive's.** The report's buckets are 1–30, 31–91, 91–180, 181–270, 271–360 (note the 31–91 overlap and the 360 ceiling), which is exactly why the system counts days from the overdue date rather than classifying from the bucket a loan sits in. The RBM return and the classification report use the day count.
- **There is a richer source we haven't pulled.** E-Banker holds `OVERDUE_DETAILS`: a per-account overdue computation with expected instalments vs actual recovery (`EXPECTED_NO_INST`, `EXPECTED_REC_AMT`, `ACTUAL_RECOVERY_AMT`, principal and interest recovery split, rescheduling date and amount, moratorium period). It isn't in the register. It would give an independent check on the instalment trigger and on the overdue date, and its `RESCHEDULEMENT_DATE/AMOUNT` columns might be where restructures are actually recorded, given the reschedule table is empty. Worth one query in the next pack (`OD_01`, the directive-relevant columns for our 18 schemes) — I'd add it to pack 3 if it hasn't gone to Barry yet, or to the next one if it has.

-- MAIIC E-Banker: pack 9 (13 October 2026) | Dupleix Institute | added 14 October
-- Read-only. Run in one SQL Developer worksheet, export the grid as CSV

-- RUN 8  |  E-Banker's own overdue computation per account  |  save as OD_01_overdue_details.csv
-- OVERDUE_DETAILS is the table behind the overdue run: for each account and
-- calculation date it carries the instalments expected and received, the
-- principal and interest recovery split, the balance, and the reschedule
-- date and amount. We hold the overdue date and the day buckets from the
-- Loan Book Report only; this gives an independent check on the days past
-- due and on the missed-instalment count, and may be where reschedules are

                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
ORDER  BY o.new_ac_number, o.ovd_calc_date, o.overdue_det_id;

-- If the schema prefix is needed, as in RUN 1: vgcbs.overdue_details and vgcbs.acmaster.

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-14 05:15:02 UTC)

The check is a two-column query — it tells you not just *whether* but *where* it's failing:

```sql
SELECT SYSDATE                              AS session_format,
       TO_CHAR(SYSDATE, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') AS forced_iso,
       1234567.89                           AS a_number
FROM dual;
```

Read the grid:

| What you see | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `session_format` = `2026-10-14 09:12:33`, same as `forced_iso` | RUN 0 took in this session | Export; the CSV should match. If it still doesn't, it's the next row |
| Grid is ISO but the **CSV** still says `10/14/2026` | The export dialog is re-formatting dates; the session setting never reaches the file | Tools → Preferences → Database → NLS → Date Format = `YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS` (type `NLS` in the Preferences search box if the node is hidden). Set once; applies to every export after |
| `session_format` = `14-OCT-26` or `10/14/2026` | RUN 0 didn't take — almost always because the ALTER lines were run in a different worksheet tab or connection | Run the two ALTER lines again in **this** tab, re-run the check, then the query |
| `a_number` = `1234567,89` | The numeric setting didn't take either | Same fix |

My guess from four packs of m/d/yyyy is the second row: Barry runs RUN 0 correctly, the grid shows ISO, and the export dialog quietly rewrites the dates. The one-time NLS preference is the fix.

**The alternative that bypasses the problem entirely:** export with SPOOL instead of the Export dialog (the BIG FILES note has the block). `SPOOL` writes what the session fetches, so RUN 0 governs it and the export dialog never gets a say. Any of the pack 9 runs can be done that way, not just the big ones — paste the ALTER lines, `SET SQLFORMAT csv`, `SPOOL <path>`, the query, `SPOOL OFF`, and run with F5.

And the honest fallback: if the dates still come out m/d/yyyy, send the files anyway. The landing accepts the declared format and records `dates_iso = no` on the load; nothing is lost, it's just a flag we'd rather see green.

Want me to drop that check query into the Pack 9 folder as `RUN 0 - check.txt` beside the others?

## 2. How the models compute ECL

All four use the same template (sheet `ECLComp`, one row per facility):

**ECL = PD x LGD x (EAD - PV(FCL))**

| Element | How it is built |
|---|---|
| EAD | Balance plus undrawn commitments (the main book includes 1,720,830,931 off-balance) |
| PV(FCL) | One cash flow of a fixed share of EAD (`$CB$7`) received 360 days after 31 Dec 2025, discounted at the facility's rate. **The share is a typed constant headed "Recovered" and labelled "From NPL": a recovery rate on non-performing loans, applied to every stage.** It is 0.4697984 (47 percent) in the main, money-market and preference-share models and 0.2 in the Mega Farm model. History: 0
| PD | Stage 1: a flat 0.03 percent for every facility in every model (S&P mapping, `PDs-S&P`); Stage 2: lifetime PD from the term structure for the years to maturity (1 to 6 on the main book); Stage 3: 100 percent; a macro adjustment from `ASS2-Macro Forecasts` |
| LGD | 1 minus discounted collateral over exposure (`ASS4-Security` haircuts and realisation periods); 100 percent when unsecured, 0 when collateral covers the exposure |
| Staging | From the past-due bracket in `PortfolioReport`; significant increase when PD doubles (multiple 2 in `AB5`) |

What that does to the numbers:

- **Main book**: Stage 1 EAD 14.0bn with ECL 1.3m (0.009 percent); Stage 2 1.14bn, ECL 63.1m (5.5 percent); Stage 3 0.95bn, ECL 424.0m (44.8 percent). **5 of the 17 Stage 3 facilities carry LGD 0** (collateral covers them), so no provision.
- **Mega Farms**: Stage 3 3,655 accounts, EAD 51.68bn, PD 100 percent and LGD 100 percent on all but one; the 20 percent repayment, discounted, is 17.4 percent of EAD, so ECL is 43.22bn (83.6 percent). Stage 1, 14 accounts, 2.42bn, ECL 0.34m.
- **Money market**: 17 placements, all Stage 1, PD 0.03 percent, LGD 100 percent, ECL 50.05m.
- **Preference shares**: five Stage 1 holdings (5.61bn, ECL 0.67m) and one Stage 3 holding in manufacturing (204.1m, ECL 116.8m, 57 percent).

import openpyxl, re, sys, glob, os
base = r"C:\Users\wadza\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\2. Documents from clients\New Doc Received 13 Oct"
files = [f for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(base, "*.xlsx")) if "ECL" in f]
KEYS = re.compile(r"(past ?due|days|dpd|classif|provision|suspense|restructur|reschedul|special mention|substandard|doubtful|loss|standard|performing|npl|directive|rbm|prudential|regulat|bracket|bucket|stage|sicr|cure|moratori|arrear)", re.I)
for f in files:
    print("=" * 100)
    print(os.path.basename(f))
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(f, data_only=False, read_only=False)
    for ws in wb.worksheets:
        print(f"--- sheet [{ws.title}] dims={ws.dimensions} max_row={ws.max_row} max_col={ws.max_column}")
    # keyword hits per sheet (limit rows scanned to 400 and cols to 60)
    for ws in wb.worksheets:
        hits = []
        for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=1, max_row=min(ws.max_row, 400), max_col=min(ws.max_column, 60)):
            for c in row:
                v = c.value
                if isinstance(v, str) and KEYS.search(v) and len(v) < 200:
                    hits.append(f"{c.coordinate}={v!r}")
        if hits:
            print(f"## [{ws.title}] {len(hits)} hits")
            for h in hits[:80]:
                print("   ", h)

import openpyxl, os, sys, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
base = r"C:\Users\wadza\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\2. Documents from clients\New Doc Received 13 Oct"
MAIN = os.path.join(base, "MAIIC & FInES ECL Model - 14th December 2025_Final.xlsx")
MEGA = os.path.join(base, "Mega Farms ECL Model - 14th December 2025_Final.xlsx")

def dump(ws, rng, label, both=None):
    print(f"\n#### {ws.title} {rng}  ({label})")
    for row in ws[rng]:
        for c in row:
            v = c.value
            if v is None:
                continue
            s = repr(v)
            if len(s) > 220:
                s = s[:220] + "..."
            extra = ""
            if both is not None:
                vv = both[ws.title][c.coordinate].value
                if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("=") and vv is not None:
                    extra = f"   -> {vv!r}"
            print(f"  {c.coordinate}: {s}{extra}")

for path, tag in [(MAIN, "MAIN"), (MEGA, "MEGA")]:
    print("\n" + "=" * 100 + f"\n{tag}: {os.path.basename(path)}")
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=False)
    wv = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
    names = wb.sheetnames
    print("sheets:", names)
    # ECLComp header block and first 3 data rows
    if "ECLComp" in names:
        ws = wb["ECLComp"]
        dump(ws, "A1:CU12", "ECLComp header rows", wv)
        dump(ws, "A13:CU15", "ECLComp first 3 facility rows (formulas -> values)", wv)
    for nm in names:
        if nm.startswith("ECLComp(InternalPDByCount"):
            dump(wb[nm], "L1:Z12", "InternalPDByCount header incl RBM Asset Classification", wv)
            dump(wb[nm], "L13:Z14", "InternalPDByCount first rows", wv)
    for nm in ["ASS1a Internal Grades-Indv Asse", "ASS1-Internal Grades", "Validation Tables", "Checklist", "Sheet2", "Closed Accounts"]:
        if nm in names:
            ws = wb[nm]
            dump(ws, f"A1:{openpyxl.utils.get_column_letter(min(ws.max_column,16))}{min(ws.max_row,62)}", nm, wv)
    if "ASS4-Security" in names:
        dump(wb["ASS4-Security"], "B1:O42", "ASS4-Security", wv)
    if "PortfolioReport" in names:
        ws = wb["PortfolioReport"]
        dump(ws, "A1:AX6", "PortfolioReport header + first data row", wv)
        dump(ws, "A7:AX8", "PortfolioReport rows 7-8", wv)
    if "Loan Book" in names:
        ws = wb["Loan Book"]
        dump(ws, "A1:AT7", "Loan Book header + first rows", wv)
        dump(ws, "S125:AT140", "Loan Book totals / NPL block", wv)
    if "KPIs" in names:
        dump(wb["KPIs"], "B2:G13", "KPIs", wv)
    if "Summary(OriginalMethod)" in names:
        dump(wb["Summary(OriginalMethod)"], "B1:O28", "Summary", wv)

````

1	<?php
2	
3	namespace App\Services\Rbm;
4	
5	use App\Services\Ebanker\LandingZoneReader;
6	use App\Services\Ebanker\LoanBookBuildService;
7	use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
8	
9	/**
10	 * The classification and provisioning return to the Reserve Bank of Malawi
11	 * (the DFI directive of 2018, section 17), PROVISIONAL LAYOUT.
12	 *
13	 * The directive requires the return "in the prescribed form"; the form
14	 * itself is MAIIC Risk's and is not yet in the repository. This service
15	 * fills the lines such a return invariably carries, from the system, in
16	 * the directive's own order: the facilities by class and term under the
17	 * directive's day bands (section 10 and 11), the minimum provision per
18	 * class (section 12) against the IFRS 9 allowance held, interest in
19	 * suspense on non-performing facilities (section 13), restructured
20	 * facilities (section 15) and the security held. When the prescribed form
21	 * arrives, LINES is re-ordered and re-worded to it line for line and the
22	 * figures stay as they are; until then every output says "provisional".
23	 *
24	 * Bands, by the term of the facility (section 2: short-term 12 months or
25	 * less; medium and long term over 12), from section 10 of the Gazette
26	 * (docs/regulatory, pages 683 and 685):
27	 *                     short-term   | medium and long
28	 *   Pass (standard)   0 to 30      | 0 to 90          provision  0 percent
29	 *   Special mention   31 to 90     | 91 to 180        provision  5 percent
30	 *   Substandard       91 to 180    | 181 to 365       provision 20 percent
31	 *   Doubtful          181 to 365   | 366 to 746       provision 50 percent
32	 *   Loss              over 365     | over 746         provision 100 percent
33	 */
34	class RbmReturnService
35	{
36	    public const CLASSES = ['Pass', 'Special mention', 'Substandard', 'Doubtful', 'Loss'];
37	    public const MINIMUM = ['Pass' => 0.00, 'Special mention' => 0.05, 'Substandard' => 0.20, 'Doubtful' => 0.50, 'Loss' => 1.00];
38	    public const BANDS = ['short' => [30, 90, 180, 365], 'long' => [90, 180, 365, 746]];
39	
40	    public function __construct(private LandingZoneReader $zone)
41	    {
42	    }
43	
44	    public static function classify(int $dpd, int $tenorMonths): string
45	    {
46	        $b = self::BANDS[$tenorMonths <= 12 ? 'short' : 'long'];
47	        if ($dpd <= $b[0]) { return 'Pass'; }
48	        if ($dpd <= $b[1]) { return 'Special mention'; }
49	        if ($dpd <= $b[2]) { return 'Substandard'; }
50	        if ($dpd <= $b[3]) { return 'Doubtful'; }
51	
52	        return 'Loss';
53	    }
54	
55	    /** @return array{period:string,status:string,sections:array,notes:list<string>} */
56	    public function build(string $period, bool $includeMegaFarm = false): array
57	    {
58	        $q = DB::table('loan_books')->where('reporting_period', $period);
59	        if (! $includeMegaFarm) {
60	            $q->whereIn('product_code', array_keys(LandingZoneReader::LOAN_GLS));
61	        }
62	        $loans = $q->get(['contract_id', 'customer_name', 'product_group', 'product_code', 'tenor', 'overdue_days', 'overdue_principal_date', 'carrying_amount', 'principal_balance', 'interest_to_date', 'ecl_value', 'ifrs9stage_post_qualitative', 'contract_status']);
63	        $notes = ['PROVISIONAL LAYOUT: the lines follow the directive\'s own order; the prescribed form from MAIIC Risk re-orders and re-words them line for line when it arrives (directive s.17).'];
64	
65	        // A. classification by class and term
66	        $a = [];
67	        foreach (self::CLASSES as $c) {
68	            foreach (['short', 'long'] as $t) {
69	                $a[$c][$t] = ['accounts' => 0, 'balance' => 0.0, 'principal' => 0.0, 'interest' => 0.0, 'ifrs9_allowance' => 0.0];
70	            }
71	        }
72	        $perLoan = [];
73	        foreach ($loans as $l) {
74	            $term = (int) $l->tenor <= 12 ? 'short' : 'long';
75	            $class = self::classify((int) $l->overdue_days, (int) $l->tenor);
76	            $a[$class][$term]['accounts']++;
77	            $a[$class][$term]['balance'] += (float) $l->carrying_amount;
78	            $a[$class][$term]['principal'] += (float) $l->principal_balance;
79	            $a[$class][$term]['interest'] += (float) ($l->interest_to_date ?? 0);
80	            $a[$class][$term]['ifrs9_allowance'] += (float) ($l->ecl_value ?? 0);
81	            $perLoan[$l->contract_id] = ['class' => $class, 'term' => $term, 'balance' => (float) $l->carrying_amount, 'dpd' => (int) $l->overdue_days, 'stage' => $l->ifrs9stage_post_qualitative];
82	        }
83	        $sectionA = [];
84	        foreach (self::CLASSES as $c) {
85	            $row = ['class' => $c, 'short_term' => $a[$c]['short'], 'medium_long_term' => $a[$c]['long']];

import openpyxl, os, glob, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
base = r"C:\Users\wadza\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\2. Documents from clients\New Doc Received 13 Oct"
files = sorted(f for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(base, "*.xlsx")) if "ECL" in f)
WANT = {
    "ECLComp": ["P2:S7", "AA2:AB5", "CA4:CB7", "N10:N22", "AX7"],
    "ECLComp(InternalPDByCount) ": ["L2:N6", "L10:N22"],
    "ASS1a Internal Grades-Indv Asse": ["B5:D12"],
    "PortfolioReport": ["AD4:AN4", "AO4:AS5", "AD5"],
    "Loan Book": ["Y3:AE5"],
    "Checklist": ["L19:M24"],
    "Sheet2": ["B2:C19"],
}
def show(wb, wv, sheet, rng):
    if sheet not in wb.sheetnames:
        print(f"  [{sheet}] missing"); return
    ws = wb[sheet]; vs = wv[sheet]
    print(f"  [{sheet}] {rng}")
    for row in ws[rng]:
        for c in row:
            if c.value is None: continue
            v = c.value; vv = vs[c.coordinate].value
            s = repr(v)[:160]
            if isinstance(v, str) and v.startswith("="):
                s += f"  -> {vv!r}"
            print(f"     {c.coordinate}: {s}")
for f in files:
    print("=" * 90); print(os.path.basename(f))
    wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(f); wv = openpyxl.load_workbook(f, data_only=True)
    for sheet, rngs in WANT.items():
        for r in rngs: show(wb, wv, sheet, r)
    # stage counts and bracket counts in ECLComp
    if "ECLComp" in wv.sheetnames:
        vs = wv["ECLComp"]; from collections import Counter
        br = Counter(); st = Counter(); rbm = Counter()
        for r in range(11, vs.max_row + 1):
            p = vs.cell(r, 16).value; s = vs.cell(r, 18).value; n = vs.cell(r, 14).value; e = vs.cell(r, 5).value
            if e is None and p is None: continue
            br[p] += 1; st[s] += 1; rbm[n] += 1
        print("  ECLComp brackets:", dict(br)); print("  ECLComp stages:", dict(st)); print("  ECLComp RBM CLASS values:", dict(rbm))

157	     *

160	    private function priorMonths(string $period, int $cureMonths, array $customers = []): array
161	    {
162	        $priorPeriod = CarbonImmutable::parse($period . '-01')->subMonth();
163	        $prior = DB::table('loan_books')->where('reporting_period', $priorPeriod->format('Y-m'))->whereNotNull('ifrs9stage_post_qualitative')
164	            ->pluck('ifrs9stage_post_qualitative', 'contract_id')->map(fn ($s) => (int) $s)->all();
165	        if ($cureMonths <= 1 || $prior === []) {
166	            return [$prior, []];
167	        }
168	        // the months whose DPD stage the count reads: the prior month back to cureMonths - 1 months ago
169	        $months = [];
170	        for ($i = 1; $i < $cureMonths; $i++) {
171	            $months[] = $priorPeriod->subMonths($i - 1)->format('Y-m');
172	        }
173	        $stored = [];
174	        foreach (DB::table('loan_books')->whereIn('reporting_period', $months)->whereIn('contract_id', array_keys($prior))->get(['contract_id', 'reporting_period', 'ifrs9stage_pre_qualitative']) as $row) {
175	            $stored[$row->contract_id][$row->reporting_period] = $row->ifrs9stage_pre_qualitative === null ? null : (int) $row->ifrs9stage_pre_qualitative;
176	        }
177	        // a month-end a qualitative trigger covered counts at the stage the trigger implied
178	        $qualByMonth = [];
179	        foreach ($months as $m) {
180	            $qualByMonth[$m] = $this->qualitative->mapAt(CarbonImmutable::parse($m . '-01')->endOfMonth()->toDateString());
181	        }
182	        $history = [];
183	        foreach ($prior as $contract => $stage) {
184	            foreach ($months as $m) {
185	                $dpdStage = $stored[$contract][$m] ?? null;
186	                if ($dpdStage !== null) {
187	                    $q = QualitativeSicrService::forLoan($qualByMonth[$m], (string) $contract, $customers[$contract] ?? null)['stage'];
188	                    $dpdStage = max($dpdStage, $q);
189	                }
190	                $history[$contract][] = $dpdStage;
191	            }
192	        }
193	
194	        return [$prior, $history];
195	    }

208	        foreach ([271 => 'arrears_271_to_360', 181 => 'arrears_180_to_270', 91 => 'arrears_91_to_180', 31 => 'arrears_30_to_90', 1 => 'arrears_1_to_30'] as $lower => $col) {
209	            $v = (float) str_replace(',', '', (string) ($r->{$col} ?? '0'));
210	            if ($v > 0) {
211	                return $lower;
212	            }
213	        }

215	        return 0;

220	    {
221	        $t = StagingThreshold::forFacility($class, $tenorMonths, $asOf?->toDateString());
222	        if ($t === null) {
223	            // no silent default (D21): a month without a rule in force is an error to fix, not a 31/181 to assume
224	            throw new \RuntimeException("No staging threshold is in force for facility class '{$class}' (tenor {$tenorMonths} months)" . ($asOf ? " at {$asOf->toDateString()}" : '') . '. Seed or approve one on the Staging & SICR Rules screen.');
225	        }

238	    /** Instalments per account from the current chart: due date and amount, in due-date order. */
239	    private function instalmentsByAccount(): array
240	    {
241	        $by = [];
242	        foreach ($this->zone->family(['P2_10']) as $row) {
243	            $p = $row['payload'];
244	            if (($p['DELETE_FLAG'] ?? 'N') === 'Y' || ($p['ACTIVE_FLAG'] ?? 'Y') !== 'Y') {
245	                continue;
246	            }
247	            $amt = (float) str_replace(',', '', (string) ($p['INSTALLMENT_AMT'] ?? '0'));
248	            if ($amt <= 0 || $row['row_date'] === null) {
249	                continue;
250	            }
251	            $by[$row['account']][] = [$row['row_date'], $amt];
252	        }
253	        foreach ($by as &$list) {
254	            usort($list, fn ($a, $b) => $a[0] <=> $b[0]);
255	        }
256	
257	        return $by;
258	    }

261	    private function receiptsByAccount(string $toDate): array
262	    {

265	            $sum = 0.0;
266	            foreach ($posts as $p) {

268	                if ($amt > 0) {

270	                }
271	            }
272	            $out[$account] = $sum;
273	        }
274

276	    }

278	    /** Receipts allocated to instalments in due-date order; the count of unpaid instalments at the end of the run. */
279	    private function consecutiveMissed(array $instalments, float $receipts, string $asOf): int
280	    {
281	        $missed = 0;
282	        foreach ($instalments as [$due, $amt]) {
283	            if ($due > $asOf) {
284	                break;
285	            }
286	            if ($receipts + 0.005 >= $amt) {
287	                $receipts -= $amt;
288	                $missed = 0;
289	            } else {

291	                $missed++;
292	            }
293	        }

import openpyxl, os, warnings
from collections import Counter
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
base = r"C:\Users\wadza\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\2. Documents from clients\New Doc Received 13 Oct"
MAIN = os.path.join(base, "MAIIC & FInES ECL Model - 14th December 2025_Final.xlsx")
MEGA = os.path.join(base, "Mega Farms ECL Model - 14th December 2025_Final.xlsx")

def num(v):
    try:
        return float(str(v).replace(",", "")) if v not in (None, "", "-") else 0.0
    except Exception:
        return 0.0

for path, tag in [(MAIN, "MAIN"), (MEGA, "MEGA")]:
    print("=" * 90, "\n", tag)
    wv = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, data_only=True)
    lb = wv["Loan Book"]
    # Loan Book: columns D(#) E(name) G(value) H(maturity) I(tenor yrs) J(morat) O(principal) S(interest) T(repay) U(carrying) Z..AE buckets
    rows = []
    for r in range(6, lb.max_row + 1):
        if lb.cell(r, 5).value is None or lb.cell(r, 4).value is None:
            continue
        if not isinstance(lb.cell(r, 4).value, (int, float)):
            continue
        rows.append(dict(r=r, name=lb.cell(r, 5).value, tenor=lb.cell(r, 9).value, morat=lb.cell(r, 10).value,
                         principal=num(lb.cell(r, 15).value), interest=num(lb.cell(r, 19).value), repay=num(lb.cell(r, 20).value), carrying=num(lb.cell(r, 21).value),
                         b1=num(lb.cell(r, 26).value), b31=num(lb.cell(r, 27).value), b91=num(lb.cell(r, 28).value), b181=num(lb.cell(r, 29).value), b271=num(lb.cell(r, 30).value), b360=num(lb.cell(r, 31).value)))
    print("loan book rows:", len(rows))
    # bucket population
    pop = Counter()
    for x in rows:
        for k in ("b1", "b31", "b91", "b181", "b271", "b360"):
            if x[k] > 0: pop[k] += 1
    print("rows with a positive amount per bucket:", dict(pop))
    # rows whose arrears sit only in 271-360 / above 360 (the revised bracket formula ignores those columns)
    missed = [x for x in rows if x["b181"] == 0 and x["b91"] == 0 and x["b31"] == 0 and (x["b271"] > 0 or x["b360"] > 0)]
    print("rows with arrears ONLY in 271-360 / above-360 (bracket formula would read 1-30):", len(missed))
    for x in missed[:15]:
        print("   ", x["r"], x["name"], "carrying", round(x["carrying"]), "271-360", round(x["b271"]), ">360", round(x["b360"]))
    # Stage 3 rows (b181>0): interest share of carrying amount (is contractual interest left in the exposure?)
    s3 = [x for x in rows if x["b181"] > 0]
    tot_c = sum(x["carrying"] for x in s3); tot_i = sum(x["interest"] for x in s3); tot_p = sum(x["principal"] for x in s3); tot_r = sum(x["repay"] for x in s3)
    print(f"bracket >181 rows: {len(s3)}  carrying {tot_c:,.0f}  principal {tot_p:,.0f}  interest-to-date {tot_i:,.0f}  repayments {tot_r:,.0f}")
    # tenor distribution
    ten = Counter()
    for x in rows:
        t = x["tenor"]
        if isinstance(t, (int, float)):
            ten["<=1y" if t <= 1 else ("1-5y" if t <= 5 else ">5y")] += 1
        else:
            ten[f"text:{t!r}"[:30]] += 1
    print("tenor (years) classes:", dict(ten))
    mor = Counter(str(x["morat"]) for x in rows)
    print("moratorium values (top 8):", mor.most_common(8))
    # Amortisation sheet 'Restructured' blocks
    am = wv["Amortisation and Repayments"]
    print("Amortisation sheet: rows with 'Restructured' label")
    for r in range(1, min(am.max_row, 4200) + 1):
        for c in range(1, 16):
            v = am.cell(r, c).value
            if isinstance(v, str) and "estructur" in v:
                ctx = [am.cell(r, cc).value for cc in range(1, 10)]
                ctx2 = [am.cell(r - 1, cc).value for cc in range(1, 10)] if r > 1 else []
                print("   ", am.cell(r, c).coordinate, ctx2, ctx)
    # 'MAIIC & FInES' sheet header
    if "MAIIC & FInES" in wv.sheetnames:
        ms = wv["MAIIC & FInES"]
        print("'MAIIC & FInES' sheet first rows:")
        for r in range(1, 8):
            print("   ", [ms.cell(r, c).value for c in range(1, 14)])
    # Summary(OriginalMethod) rows 3-9 and 13-26 values
    sm = wv["Summary(OriginalMethod)"]
    print("Summary(OriginalMethod) B3:O9")
    for r in range(3, 10):
        print("   ", [sm.cell(r, c).value for c in range(2, 16)])

81	**2. Definitions: short-, medium- and long-term facilities** - *Done*
82	
83	- **What it requires:** A short-term facility has a repayment period of not more than 12 months; medium-term more than 12 and up to 60; long-term more than 60.
84	- **What the engine does:** The staging thresholds are keyed by facility class and the tenor in months: DEFAULT with min_tenor 0 (short-term, 91 days) and min_tenor 13 (medium and long, 181 days), each row citing the directive's section 2; the loan book carries the tenor from the loan master.
85	- **Compliance comment:** Compliant.

92	
93	**9. Classification of credit facilities** - *Done*
94	
95	- **What it requires:** Classify every facility as pass, special mention, substandard, doubtful or loss by the days in arrears and the qualitative factors.
96	- **What the engine does:** The RBM Classification report classifies each loan from the days past due the build counts from the oldest overdue instalment, under the directive's bands by term of facility (the same bands as the RBM Return, proven to agree at every band edge); the arrears ageing shows the class beside each day band; the IFRS 9 stage is mapped to the RBM class in the IFRS 9 vs RBM report.
97	- **Compliance comment:** Compliant.

103	**10. Non-performing: substandard from 91 days (short-term) or 181 days (medium and long term)** - *Done*
104	
105	- **What it requires:** A facility is non-performing when principal or interest is due and unpaid for 90 days or more on a short-term facility, or 180 days or more on a medium- or long-term facility.
106	- **What the engine does:** Stage 3 from 91 days for a facility of 12 months or less and from 181 days otherwise; the November 2025 model's uniform 181 days and the accounting policy's 90 days are compared in spec section 3.6 and the thresholds carry the comparison as their rebuttal basis.
107	- **General comment:** The LONG_TERM proposal (91 days for every class) is seeded future-dated and inactive pending CFO sign-off.
108	- **Compliance comment:** Compliant.

115	
116	- **What it requires:** Doubtful from 181 (short-term) or 366 days (medium and long term); loss beyond 365 or 746 days, or where recovery is not expected.
117	- **What the engine does:** The RBM Classification report and the RBM Return apply the doubtful and loss bands by term from section 10 of the Gazette (181/366 days short-term, 366/747 otherwise); the loan book's buckets end at 271 to 360 days and the build counts days from the overdue date without a ceiling, so the bands are classified from the day count; the qualitative 'recovery not expected' flag is the write-off policy MAIIC has not stated.
118	- **Compliance comment:** Partially done: the day bands are applied; the qualitative loss criterion awaits the policy.

129	- **Compliance comment:** Compliant in the report; the eligible-security netting rests on the collateral register (IFRS 7 workbook F1).

## CLAUDE  (2026-10-14 05:31:41 UTC)

Comparison done. Here is what the December 2025 workbooks do with the directive against what the system does.

**Written for:** you (chat answer); I can save it as a note beside the colleague's evaluation in `New Doc Received 13 Oct` if you want colleagues to pick it up.

## Bottom line

The December models carry the directive's vocabulary but do not apply it. Every sheet has an "RBM CLASS" column, an "RBM Asset Classification - FDIs" table (short/medium/long, NPL threshold 91-180 / >181) and an ASS4 block headed "BASED ON RBM SEGMENTATION - NOT BEING USED", and in all four files the RBM CLASS column evaluates to 0 on every row, the NPL Flag column is empty, and the provision rates 0/5/20/50/100 appear nowhere. What the models actually do is one ageing ladder for every facility regardless of term (1-30 → Stage 1, 31-90 and 91-180 → Stage 2, >181 → Stage 3), read from the Loan Book Report's arrears buckets. The system applies the directive by term, counts days, produces the five classes, the minimum provisions, the higher-of, and the suspense line.

## Section by section

| Directive (Gazette pp. 680-685) | December 2025 models | System | Difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| **s.2 term classes**: short ≤12 months, medium 12-60, long >60 | Table exists (`Facility_Tenor_Class`: 0→short, 1→medium, 6→long, so "long" starts at 6 years not 5) but nothing reads it; Mega Farm tenor is text (`5.00 (Cap+Int)`) so `YEARFRAC` is `#VALUE!` on all 3,675 rows | `tenor` in months from the loan master; ≤12 short, else medium/long (`StagingThresholdSeeder`, `RbmReturnService::classify`) | Model: term never applied. System: applied. |
| **s.10 classification**: short 30/90/180/365; medium-long 90/180/365/746 | One ladder: 1-30, 31-90, 91-180, >181. Nothing above 181 is distinguished, so substandard/doubtful/loss cannot be told apart. Short-term facilities (2 term loans; all 19 money-market placements at 0.08-0.5 yr) default at >181 instead of 91 | Five classes by term: Dec 2025 main book = Pass 68, Special mention 13, Substandard 15, Doubtful 17, Loss 10 (123 loans) | Model collapses three NPL classes into one and uses the medium/long line for short-term paper. |
| **Days past due basis** | Highest non-empty arrears bucket of the Loan Book Report (`PortfolioReport!AP`). The "revised formula" reads only the 1-30, 31-90, 91-180, 181-270 columns; the 271-360 and >360 columns are ignored (no row affected at Dec 2025 because the report fills nothing beyond 181-270) | Days from `OVERDUE_PRINCI_DATE` under governed `dpd_basis` (77 of 123 loans at Dec 2025), bucket lower bound only as fallback | Model has no day count at all; system does. At Dec 2025 the system counts 42 loans ≥181 days (26 >365, 9 >746) where the model has 18 at ">181". |
| **s.11 quarterly review; large exposures individually** | Annual (31 Dec); "Individual assessment? = Y" on every corporate row, which is a flag not a review | Monthly build and staging; period lock | Frequency: model annual, system monthly. |
| **s.12 write-off of loss facilities in the following quarter** | No loss class, so no trigger; a `Closed Accounts` list only | Loss class is identified; write-offs come from the ledger (type 300). The system reports the class, it does not enforce the quarter rule | Neither enforces s.12; only the system can identify the loans it applies to. |
| **s.13 non-accrual**: cease accruing, reverse uncollected interest, cash basis, regardless of collateral | Exposure = principal + interest to date − repayments. On the 18 NPLs: carrying 941.3m = principal 1,212.2m + interest 913.8m − repayments 1,184.7m. Accrued interest stays in EAD; no suspense anywhere (the only "suspense" strings are template instrument types) | Stage 3 interest on the net basis in the EIR roll-forward; the contractual interest E-Banker keeps posting is reported as interest in suspense (RBM return section C, GL reconciliation) | Model ignores s.13; system computes and reports it. |
| **s.13(3) restore to accrual only when all past-due principal and interest paid** | Point-in-time bracket; a loan drops to Stage 1 the moment its bucket clears | Governed cure: held at the prior stage until 3 consecutive month-ends below the threshold (`stage_cure_months`) | Both differ from the directive's "all arrears paid" test; the system's is the stricter and governed one. Worth a note in the rebuttal basis. |
| **s.14 + Schedule: minimum provisions 0/5/20/50/100** | Not applied. ECL = PD × LGD × (EAD − PV of a typed recovery share: 47% main/MM/pref, 20% Mega Farm) | Minimum per class on the gross balance against the IFRS 9 allowance, shortfall per class, higher-of (`RbmReturnService` B, `provisionComparison`); eligible-security netting still open | Model has no prudential floor. |
| **s.15 excess of prudential over IFRS → loan-loss reserve appropriation** | Nothing | `higher_of_the_two` computed; no appropriation journal | System computes the excess; the reserve entry is not built in either. |
| **s.16(1) restructuring needs Board approval** | Four "Restructured" amortisation blocks (Chikho Hotel, MUSECO, Corran Farming, one unnamed; effective May/Sept 2022) hand-built; no register, no classification effect | Register awaited (Reschedule Report / OD_01 columns); modification test governed | Open on both sides. |
| **Mega Farm** | 3,646 of 3,675 accounts at >181 (the ECLComp sheet says 3,660; the two sheets disagree by 14 accounts); PD 100%, LGD 100%, 20% recovery share; no term class | `MEGA_FARM` threshold 31/91 as short-term seasonal finance; no Dec 2025 Mega Farm rows in the bootstrap DB yet (five MF files still missing) | Same outcome in December (all Stage 3 either way); the system's short-term assumption contradicts the model's own book where the first rows are 5-year facilities, so the Mega Farm tenor needs confirming from M09. |

Where they agree: both put 31 days past due in Stage 2 (IFRS 9 presumption kept, although the directive's standard band for medium/long runs to 90), both treat >181 as default for medium and long term, and both ignore collateral when deciding non-performing status.

## Same-date numbers, December 2025 main book

| | Model (14 Jan version) | System (bootstrap) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Facilities | 108 | 123 |
| Stage 1 / 2 / 3 | 80 / 10 / 18 | 50 / 22 / 51 |
| ≥181 days past due | 18 (bracket) | 42 (day count) |
| Gross on-balance | 14.70bn | 14.84bn |
| ECL | 488.5m | 4.03bn (bootstrap PD/LGD, not approved parameters, so not comparable as a number) |

The staging gap (18 vs 51 in Stage 3) is the practical difference that matters: the system counts from the oldest unpaid instalment (max 1,765 days), the model from the report's bucket, and nothing today proves which basis E-Banker's own overdue run agrees with. That is exactly what pack 9 RUN 8 (OD_01) was added for, so no new request to Barry.

## Three labelling errors on our side I found while reading the Gazette

The directive's actual numbering is: s.10 classification, s.11 review, s.12 write-offs, s.13 income recognition, s.14 provisions (Schedule), s.15 loan-loss reserve, s.16 restrictions (restructuring, 25% single borrower, no overdrafts), s.17-18 penalties. There is no "return" section; s.15(3) only says loan-loss reserves go on the call report.

1. [RbmReturnService.php:11-19](C:/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9/app/Services/Rbm/RbmReturnService.php#L11-L19) cites "section 17" for the return and "section 15" for restructured facilities; both wrong.
2. [RBM_DFI_Directive_2018_Compliance_Audit.md](C:/xampp/htdocs/MAICC-IFRS9/docs/compliance/RBM_DFI_Directive_2018_Compliance_Audit.md) numbers classification as 9, provisions as 12, restructuring as 15, returns as 17, and states that s.15 requires a restructured facility to "keep its classification"; the Gazette has no such clause (s.16(1) only requires Board approval).
3. The same audit lists "s.13 cure = all arrears paid" nowhere; the system's 3-month cure should be recorded against s.13(3) as a rebuttal, not left silent.

Say the word and I will correct the section references in the service comment, the compliance audit (md and xlsx), and the spec where it repeats them, and add the s.13(3) note.

"""Render a .sql run sheet to a monospace A4 PDF with a title band and page numbers."""
import sys, textwrap
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.lib.units import mm
from reportlab.lib import colors
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

src, out, title, sub = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
lines = open(src, encoding="utf-8").read().splitlines()
W, H = A4
left, top, bottom = 16 * mm, H - 22 * mm, 16 * mm
font, size, lead = "Courier", 8.2, 10.2
maxw = 108  # characters per line at this size

def header(c, page):
    c.setFillColor(colors.HexColor("#0b2b1a")); c.rect(0, H - 14 * mm, W, 14 * mm, fill=1, stroke=0)
    c.setFillColor(colors.white); c.setFont("Helvetica-Bold", 10); c.drawString(left, H - 9 * mm, title)
    c.setFont("Helvetica", 7.5); c.drawRightString(W - left, H - 9 * mm, sub)
    c.setFillColor(colors.HexColor("#666666")); c.setFont("Helvetica", 7.5)
    c.drawString(left, 9 * mm, "Read-only queries. Run RUN 0 first. One CSV per query, named as shown.")
    c.drawRightString(W - left, 9 * mm, "Page %d" % page)
    c.setFillColor(colors.black); c.setFont(font, size)

c = canvas.Canvas(out, pagesize=A4); page = 1; header(c, page); y = top
for raw in lines:
    pieces = textwrap.wrap(raw, maxw, subsequent_indent="       ", drop_whitespace=False) or [""]
    for piece in pieces:
        if y < bottom + lead:
            c.showPage(); page += 1; header(c, page); y = top
        if raw.lstrip().startswith("-- RUN") or raw.startswith("--====") or raw.lstrip().startswith("-- "):
            c.setFillColor(colors.HexColor("#1f5f3f") if raw.lstrip().startswith("-- RUN") else colors.HexColor("#555555"))
            if raw.lstrip().startswith("-- RUN"): c.setFont("Courier-Bold", size)
        else:
            c.setFillColor(colors.black)
        c.drawString(left, y, piece); c.setFont(font, size); y -= lead
c.save(); print("written", out, "pages", page)

--- content ---
-- MAIIC E-Banker: pack 9 (13 October 2026) | Dupleix Institute | RUN 8 added 14 October, SPLIT INTO 8a, 8b, 8c the same day
-- Read-only. Run in one SQL Developer worksheet, export the grid as CSV
-- (header row, comma, strings in double quotes, UTF-8), named as below.
-- Session settings first (RUN 0), in the same worksheet: put the cursor on
-- each ALTER SESSION line and press Ctrl+Enter, then run the SELECT. The
-- file received this morning has dates as 8/8/2025, so RUN 0 had not run.
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_DATE_FORMAT = 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS';
ALTER SESSION SET NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS = '.,';

-- WHY RUN 8 WAS SPLIT (14 October, afternoon)
--   The single query stopped with "Result set exceeds the maximum size
--   (100 MB)" and the export holds 21 rows of one account. The table is big
--   because the overdue run is DAILY since 14 July 2025 (one row per account
--   per day; month-end rows only before that, back-filled on 8 to 11 August
--   2025). So it is split: a profile (8a) that sizes it, the month-end rows
--   (8b) that the system compares with, and the daily rows by quarter with
--   the columns that matter (8c), each well under the limit. The 21-row file
--   is superseded; please leave it, we will not load it.
--
-- Why this table at all (unchanged from the morning):
--   1. Today every arrears figure the system holds comes from the stored
--      Loan Book Report (P2_08): the overdue date and five day buckets, as
--      the report computed them on the day it was run. The staging engine
--      counts days past due from that overdue date (the directive's basis)
--      and only falls back to the bucket when the date is blank. There is no
--      second source to check it against. OVERDUE_DETAILS is the table the
--      overdue run itself writes: per account and calculation date, the
--      instalments expected and received, the principal and interest
--      recovery split, the balance. It is the independent check on the days
--      past due and on the four-missed-instalments trigger (spec 3.6, D31),
--      which today is rebuilt from the instalment chart and the ledger.
--   2. Its RESCHEDULEMENT_DATE and RESCHEDULEMENT_AMOUNT columns may be where
--      a restructure is actually recorded in E-Banker: LOAN_RESCHEDULE_DETAILS
--      is empty (6 October dictionary), the vendor's Reschedule Report is still
--      owed, and the directive's section 16 and the 10 percent modification
--      test (spec 3.3.2) both wait on restructure history. If these columns
--      carry it, that request to the vendor can be dropped.
--   3. The report's buckets are 1-30, 31-91, 91-180, 181-270, 271-360 (note
--      the overlap at 91 and the ceiling at 360); the directive's bands run
--      to 365 and 746 by term. A per-account day count from this table lets
--      the RBM return be checked without the buckets.
-- GOAL, and what to do with the files once they are back (for whoever lands them):
--   a. Land 8b as query id OD_01 and the 8c files as OD_02 (both registered in
--      EbankerQuerySeeder, key OVERDUE_DET_ID, account NEW_AC_NUMBER, date
--      OVD_CALC_DATE, incremental; a row in both is landed once) through the
--      feed like any extract: eir:land-pack, or the Feed screen. 8a is a
--      profile: read it, do not land it.
--   b. Per account and month-end (8b), compare the days past due the overdue
--      run implies (OVD_CALC_DATE less OVERDUE_PRINCI_DATE, and its own
--      OVERDUE_PERIOD column, which is in months: 4.97 on 31 Dec 2024 for an
--      overdue date of 1 Aug 2024) with loan_books.overdue_days from the
--      Loan Book Report. Report the count that agree and list the rest. A
--      systematic difference means one of the two bases is wrong.
--   c. Compare EXPECTED_NO_INST against the instalments actually received
--      (ACTUAL_RECOVERY_AMT, PRINCIPLE/INTEREST_RECOVERY_AMT) with the
--      four-missed-instalments trigger StagingService rebuilds from P2_10 and
--      the ledger: the loans the trigger lifts to Stage 3 should be the loans
--      this table shows four or more instalments behind.
--   d. If RESCHEDULEMENT_DATE / RESCHEDULEMENT_AMOUNT are populated for any of
--      our accounts, that is the restructure history: list the accounts with
--      the dates and amounts, and raise it as the input for the restructured
--      loan register (directive s.16(1)) and the 10 percent modification test
--      (spec 3.3.2); then tell Barry the vendor's Reschedule Report is no
--      longer needed. If they are empty on every row, say so and the
--      vendor request stands. (On the 21 rows received they are empty / 0.00.)
--   e. Record the outcome in the pack review note (as Pack 7 results review
--      does): rows, accounts, date range, the tie counts of b and c, the
--      answer to d.
-- If the schema prefix is needed, as in RUN 1: vgcbs.overdue_details and vgcbs.acmaster.


-- RUN 8a  |  profile of the overdue table: rows per calculation month  |  save as OD_00_overdue_profile.csv
-- A few dozen rows. Tells us how many rows each month holds and how many
-- accounts, so we know every later file is complete. Run first.
SELECT TO_CHAR(TRUNC(o.ovd_calc_date, 'MM'), 'YYYY-MM')  AS calc_month,
       COUNT(*)                                            AS rows_in_month,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.new_ac_number)                     AS accounts,
       COUNT(DISTINCT TRUNC(o.ovd_calc_date))              AS calc_days,
       MIN(o.ovd_calc_date)                                AS first_calc_date,
       MAX(o.ovd_calc_date)                                AS last_calc_date,
       SUM(CASE WHEN o.rescheduLement_date IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS rows_with_reschedule_date
FROM   overdue_details o
WHERE  o.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
GROUP  BY TRUNC(o.ovd_calc_date, 'MM')
ORDER  BY 1;


-- RUN 8b  |  the overdue computation at each MONTH-END, every account, all dates  |  save as OD_01_overdue_details.csv
-- Only the rows whose calculation date is the last day of a month: about
-- 120 accounts x 24 months, a few thousand rows, all 78 columns. These are
-- the rows the system compares with its month-end loan book.
SELECT o.*
FROM   overdue_details o
WHERE  o.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
AND    TRUNC(o.ovd_calc_date) = TRUNC(LAST_DAY(o.ovd_calc_date))
ORDER  BY o.new_ac_number, o.ovd_calc_date, o.overdue_det_id;


-- RUN 8c  |  the DAILY overdue rows, one quarter per file, 34 columns  |  save as OD_02_overdue_daily_<quarter>.csv
-- Six queries, identical except for the two dates and the file name. Each
-- is about 120 accounts x 92 days, roughly 11,000 rows and 3 MB. Run and
-- export them one at a time. If a quarter still trips the 100 MB message,
-- SPOOL it instead (see "BIG FILES - export with SPOOL" in the pack 3 folder).

-- RUN 8c-1  |  save as OD_02_overdue_daily_2025Q3.csv  (daily rows start 14 July 2025)
SELECT o.overdue_det_id, o.op_branch_mst_id, o.transaction_date, o.ovd_calc_date, o.glcode,
       o.new_ac_number, o.sub_ac_number, o.scheme_mst_id, o.installment_amt, o.installment_start_date,
       o.reschedulement_date, o.reschedulement_amount, o.moratorium_period, o.rate_of_interest, o.expiry_date,
       o.balance, o.expected_no_inst, o.expected_rec_amt, o.actual_recovery_amt, o.total_recovery_amount,
       o.principle_recovery_amt, o.interest_recovery_amt, o.overdue_amount, o.overdue_principle, o.overdue_interest,
       o.overdue_princi_date, o.overdue_int_date, o.last_cr_date, o.last_cr_amount, o.overdue_installment,
       o.overdue_period, o.status_due_flag, o.delete_flag, o.operation_date
FROM   overdue_details o
WHERE  o.new_ac_number IN (SELECT a.new_ac_number FROM acmaster a
                           WHERE a.scheme_mst_id IN (84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,140,141,142,143,144,145))
AND    o.ovd_calc_date >= DATE '2025-07-01' AND o.ovd_calc_date < DATE '2025-10-01'
ORDER  BY o.new_ac_number, o.ovd_calc_date, o.overdue_det_id;

-- RUN 8c-2  |  save as OD_02_overdue_daily_2025Q4.csv
SELECT o.overdue_det_id, o.op_branch_mst_id, o.transaction_date, o.ovd_calc_date, o.glcode,

       o.overdue_princi_date, o.overdue_int_date, o.last_cr_date, o.last_cr_amount, o.overdue_installment,

"""Splice the split RUN 8 into the pack 9 all-runs sheet, update the README, copy to the repo, render the PDF."""
import re, shutil, subprocess, sys
from pathlib import Path
P9 = Path(r"C:\Users\wadza\OneDrive\2026\Projects\MAIIC\2. Documents from clients\Raw Query Scripts\Query Requests to MAIIC\Received 12 October 2026\Pack 4\Pack 9")
REPO = Path(r"C:\xampp\htdocs\MAICC-IFRS9")
run8 = (P9 / "RUN 8 - OD_01_overdue_details.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
allruns = P9 / "FOLLOW-UP extracts for Barry - pack 9 - 13 Oct 2026 (all runs).sql"
txt = allruns.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

# the RUN 8 section of the sheet = everything from the RUN 8 banner to the end
i = txt.index("-- RUN 8  |")
head = txt[:i]
# the run-8 file minus its own 8-line preamble (banner, export note, ALTER SESSION lines)
body = run8.split("ALTER SESSION SET NLS_NUMERIC_CHARACTERS = '.,';\n", 1)[1].lstrip("\n")
section = "-- RUN 8  |  E-Banker's own overdue computation per account  |  SPLIT into 8a, 8b, 8c (14 October, afternoon)\n" + body
txt = head + section
# the preamble's run list: add the RUN 8 lines after RUN 7 if not there
old = "--   RUN 7       GL_OPENING_BALANCE_BK240824, the GL at the migration\n"
new = old + ("--   RUN 8a      OVERDUE_DETAILS, a profile by month (added 14 October)\n"
             "--   RUN 8b      OVERDUE_DETAILS, the month-end rows, all 78 columns\n"
             "--   RUN 8c-1..6 OVERDUE_DETAILS, the daily rows since July 2025, one quarter per file\n")
if "RUN 8a      OVERDUE_DETAILS" not in txt:
    assert old in txt, "run list anchor"
    txt = txt.replace(old, new, 1)
txt = txt.replace("--   RUN 8       OVERDUE_DETAILS, the overdue run per account (added 14 October)\n", "")
allruns.write_text(txt, encoding="utf-8")
print("all-runs sheet:", len(txt.splitlines()), "lines")

# README
rd = P9 / "README.txt"
r = rd.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
r = re.sub(r"  RUN 8 - OD_01_overdue_details\.sql.*\n",
           "  RUN 8 - OD_01_overdue_details.sql   (added 14 Oct, SPLIT the same afternoon: 8a profile -> OD_00,\n"
           "                                       8b month-end rows -> OD_01, 8c-1..6 daily rows by quarter -> OD_02_..._<quarter>;\n"
           "                                       the single query exceeded SQL Developer's 100 MB limit, the 21-row\n"
           "                                       OD_01 file of 14 Oct 09:09 is a fragment and is superseded)\n", r)
if "SPLIT the same afternoon" not in r:
    r += "\n  RUN 8 (split 14 Oct afternoon): 8a profile -> OD_00, 8b month-end rows -> OD_01, 8c-1..6 daily rows by quarter -> OD_02_<quarter>.\n"
rd.write_text(r, encoding="utf-8")
print("README updated")

# repo copies

dst = REPO / "docs/bootstrap/queries/Pack 9 - 13 Oct 2026 (all runs).sql"

                     capture_output=True, text=True)
print(out.stdout, out.stderr)

<?php
// Dump the take-on postings (31 Jul 2024, types 301/303/305) per account from the landed ledger, plus the loan master names.
use App\Services\Ebanker\LandingZoneReader;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

$zone = new LandingZoneReader();
$out = [];
foreach ($zone->ledgerByAccount('2024-08-05') as $account => $posts) {
    foreach ($posts as $p) {
        $pl = $p['payload'];
        $t = (string) ($pl['TRANTYPE'] ?? '');
        $d = substr((string) $p['row_date'], 0, 10);
        if ($d >= '2024-07-25' && $d <= '2024-08-05' && in_array($t, ['301', '303', '305'], true)) {
            $out[$account][$t] = ($out[$account][$t] ?? 0) + (float) str_replace(',', '', (string) ($pl['TRANSAMT'] ?? 0));
            $out[$account]['date'] = $d;
            $out[$account]['narr'] = substr((string) ($pl['NARRATION'] ?? ($pl['PARTICULARS'] ?? '')), 0, 60);
        }
    }
}
$gl = [];
foreach (DB::table('loan_books')->where('reporting_period', '2024-07')->get(['contract_id', 'customer_name', 'product_code', 'carrying_amount', 'principal_balance', 'interest_to_date']) as $r) {
    $gl[ltrim($r->contract_id, '0')] = ['name' => $r->customer_name, 'gl' => $r->product_code, 'carrying' => (float) $r->carrying_amount, 'principal' => (float) $r->principal_balance, 'interest' => (float) $r->interest_to_date];
}
file_put_contents('C:/Users/wadza/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--xampp-htdocs-Stress-Testing-App/ee984144-7b28-4df1-9a6e-560f112869e9/scratchpad/takeon.json', json_encode(['postings' => $out, 'book_2024_07' => $gl], JSON_PRETTY_PRINT));
echo 'accounts with take-on postings: ' . count($out) . "; book rows Jul 2024: " . count($gl) . "\n";

````
